claims.statement: prepare_environment runs as a setup job: the webview mints a UUID job id before invoking, TauriBackend.prepare always sends huggingFaceToken: null, and Application::prepare fills a missing token from settings, loads the saved EnginePreset, and claims the single job slot (BUSY on conflict) before delegating through EnginePort to setup::prepare.
When the saved preset's recomputed EnvironmentStatus::is_ready() already holds, setup::prepare emits a ready phase at 100% and returns the current status without spawning uv or the worker.

setup::prepare branches per preset: WhisperX installs engine/.venv from requirements.lock with --require-hashes, then imports the standard Hugging Face cache, may enable offline flags, and runs worker prepare; Qwen3 installs engine/qwen3/.venv from requirements-qwen3.lock and goes straight to worker prepare. Every stage re-runs status() so only missing work executes.

Engine install runs `uv python install 3.12` (into UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR), `uv venv --clear --python 3.12` (replacing partial venvs left by failed attempts so retries are idempotent), and `uv pip install -r <lock>` under UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed, with the readiness marker written only after pip exits successfully.

AppPaths::resolve places the Qwen3 stack in its own virtualenv at engine/qwen3/ so the pinned WhisperX environment never shares dependency versions, with per-preset interpreters, marker files, model manifests, and engine bin dirs; the HF/torch/uv caches and the uv-managed interpreter pool sit under the app data root so removing Galpi's folder reclaims the gigabytes.

Readiness markers record `<version>+<requirements-hash>`, where the hash is an FNV-1a fingerprint of worker/requirements.txt or worker/requirements-qwen3.txt computed at compile time by build.rs (GALPI_WHISPERX_REQUIREMENTS_HASH / GALPI_QWEN3_REQUIREMENTS_HASH), so editing a pin invalidates every existing virtualenv on its own and the next prepare reinstalls the venv and rewrites the marker.

The uv binary is a checksum-pinned sidecar: uv_binary() resolves src-tauri/binaries/uv-aarch64-apple-darwin in debug builds and a uv beside the executable in release builds; scripts/stage-sidecars.ts stages it by verifying SHA-256 of both the release archive and the extracted binary against pinned constants and skips the download when a staged binary still matches.

process_environment builds each spawned process's entire environment deterministically rather than inheriting the shell: app-local HF_HOME, TORCH_HOME, UV_CACHE_DIR and UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR, PYTHONPATH at the worker root, ko_KR.UTF-8 locale, telemetry-off flags, PATH with the preset's engine bin dir first (so the linked ffmpeg resolves), and HF_TOKEN inserted only when a trimmed non-empty token is supplied.

WhisperX prepare imports the three known model directories from ~/.cache/huggingface/hub into the app cache before touching the network: files are hard-linked with a copy fallback, symlinks are recreated only when their canonical target stays inside the source repository (an escaping link is an error), existing destination files are skipped, and an import failure is emitted as a stderr log event and treated as zero imported so prepare continues to the normal download path.

can_use_offline_cache is true only when all three model directories imported and no non-blank Hugging Face token is configured; when true the model environment gains HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1, because a complete tokenless cache needs no network and a token would suggest the user intends gated access.

When models or ffmpeg are missing, the host spawns `<preset python> -m galpi_worker prepare --manifest <manifest> --engine-bin <bin> --engine <preset>` with worker_protocol: true so stdout parses as the JSONL protocol; the worker CLI routes prepare to prepare_models, and any worker exception still reaches the host as exactly one error protocol event via the main() catch-all.

The worker's first prepare act is link_ffmpeg: it links the imageio-ffmpeg binary into the engine's bin dir, replacing an existing link and falling back to a copy with mode 0o755 when symlinking fails. That single file is exactly what the ffmpeg_ready readiness check inspects and what process_environment's PATH resolves for every later ffmpeg invocation.

Qwen3 prepare downloads the Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-1.7B and Qwen/Qwen3-ForcedAligner-0.6B snapshots concurrently (two workers) and a DownloadReporter subclasses tqdm to sum every per-file bar into one models-band phase event mapped onto 10–40% with a GB message, throttled to at most one event per second and reporting only counted bytes against known totals — never a fabricated ETA — because a silent multi-GB download would make the app look stalled.

Qwen3 prepare converts the ASR snapshot to 8-bit MLX weights (group size 64) into cache/mlx/qwen3-asr-1.7b-8bit: conversion is skipped when the weights file already exists, otherwise it builds a sibling .partial staging directory (wiping any stale one), writes the quantized safetensors plus tokenizer/config sidecars and quantization_config.json, and moves it into place with os.replace so a crash never leaves a half-built model the readiness gate would mistake for a complete one.

verify_qwen3_session loads the converted weights via Session(model=<dir>) and transcribes one second of silence, first checking weights.safetensors exists so a missing conversion yields an actionable error instead of a repo-id validation message; this moves bad-conversion and missing-runtime-dependency failures from a real meeting into the prepare step whose job is to report them.

The worker writes its models manifest atomically (a .tmp file plus replace) with protocol: 1 and version strings; the host then recomputes readiness by parsing the manifest (protocol == 1, whisperx == "3.8.6" / qwen3 == "2"), checking the expected models--Org--Name hub directories and, for Qwen3, the MLX weights file — so anything short of full readiness fails with SETUP_INCOMPLETE regardless of the worker's exit code.

All prepare progress surfaces as WorkerEvent::Phase JSONL through the same JobEvents bridge transcription uses: the host's emit_phase (engine 5/22/35%, models 45/50%, ready 100%) and the worker's phase events share one enum; TauriEvents re-emits each as a job-event Tauri event, and the webview reduces them with the same reduceJobEvent state machine that drives the setup progress card, percent, log disclosure, and the engine→models phase rail.

run_process batches the worker's stderr — thousands of lines from uv pip installs and model downloaders — into a single log event every 100 ms or 32 lines (whichever first), keeps a 20-line tail whose last line becomes the PROCESS_FAILED detail on non-zero exit, and rejects lines above a 64 KiB bound so the webview is never flooded.

A failed prepare is safe to retry: status() gates each stage so completed work is skipped (an existing venv whose marker matches the compiled fingerprint is reused as-is), uv venv --clear replaces partial venvs, markers are written only after pip succeeds, MLX conversion is skipped or atomic, link_ffmpeg replaces an existing link, the WhisperX cache import skips existing files, and interrupted Hugging Face downloads resume from the app cache.

The Hugging Face token reaches only the model-download environment: Application::prepare fills a missing request token from settings (pinned by a unit test), setup::prepare builds the install environment with None and only the model environment with HF_TOKEN (trimmed, non-empty), and every transcription environment is built with None — Qwen3 transcription additionally forces HF_HUB_OFFLINE/TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE so no network round trip occurs and the token never rides along to inference.

The webview never handles a stored token's value: the host exposes only a hugging_face_token_stored boolean, TokenSettingsView keeps the field read-only and masked while stored (changing a stored token means clearing and retyping), and the token-guide popover walks first-time users through accepting the gated pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1 terms and minting a fine-grained read-only hf_ token, noting the token can be left empty once access is approved or the model is already on the Mac.

Focused tests pin the flow's invariants: the model-cache import uses hard links and preserves only in-repo symlinks, and offline mode requires the complete tokenless cache; Qwen3 model ids keep the Qwen/… repo-id shape cache_dir_name relies on; prepare fills the saved token and prepares the saved preset rather than a default; and closing the token-guide popover from inside returns focus to its trigger.
